question: Fifteen people dead, including firefighters, three of them in Greece, dozens injured, hundreds of homes and properties destroyed and 4.3 million acres of torched land is the toll of the fires in France, Spain, and Greece, so far. In Greece, enormous destruction was caused in Rethymno, Boeotia, Paros, and Poikilo Oros in Attica.

Both here and throughout the EU, unified firefighting planning with a primary focus on prevention is an ‘unknown concept’. As for the much-vaunted rescEU, in practice it legitimises and perpetuates the shortage of personnel, firefighting equipment and infrastructure. In view of the above: 1.

What is the Commission’s position on the request for the victims of the fires in Greece, Spain, France and other countries to be compensated immediately – for 100% of the damage they suffered – from the EUSF, bypassing the unacceptable conditions that exclude them?

What is the Commission’s position on the fact that the rescEU mechanism aims to recycle a minimum of fire-fighting equipment from country to country, since covering needs at national level is ruled out on the basis of the cost-benefit criterion?

What is the Commission’s position on the fact that the development of a unified fire protection plan with an emphasis on prevention, the organisation of ground forces within the framework of integrated forest management and protection and firefighting and the staffing of Fire Brigades and Forest Services with all the required personnel are considered unnecessary costs – and therefore not prioritised – within the framework of EU policy that endangers people, public property and the environment?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.10.2026) The Commission stands ready to support and guide the national authorities should they wish to apply for support under the EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF).

However, the EUSF can only be activated at the request of Greece with a deadline of 12 weeks from the first damage, demonstrating that the total direct damage exceeds the thresholds specified in Article 2 Regulation (EC) 2012/20021. The EUSF may cover a part of the costs for emergency and recovery operations incurred by public authorities2.

While the EU has a supporting competence in the area of civil protection, Member States are primarily responsible. This includes preventing and protecting against natural or man-made disasters and allocating the necessary resources for the organisation and staffing of fire and forest services.

The strategic reserve of European disaster response capabilities and stockpiles rescEU3 is created as an additional safety net to provide assistance only in overwhelming situations where capacities at national levels are not, in the circumstances, able to ensure an effective response.

Since 2019, the EU is developing the rescEU permanent aerial firefighting fleet, funded the purchase of 12 fire-fighting aircraft and five helicopters, and is looking at ways to further develop these capacities in the future. The Commission attaches great importance to wildfire prevention, preparedness and risk reduction and to the protection of people, ecosystems and rural economies.

On this line the recent Communication on an integrated approach to wildfire risk management4 proposes precisely a holistic approach covering prevention, preparedness, response and recovery. At EU level, the Commission supports Member States through policy guidance, funding, and capacity-building.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002 of 11 November 2002 establishing the European Union Solidarity

Fund (OJ L 311, 14.11.2002, p. 3) as amended by Regulation (EU) No 661/2014 of the European Parliament and the Council of 15 May 2014 (OJ L 189, 27.6.2014, p. 143) and by Regulation (EU) 2020/461 of the European Parliament and the Council of 30 March 2020 (OJ L 99, 31.3.2020, p. 9: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:32002R2012).

2 This means, for example, the recovery of essential infrastructure, provision of temporary accommodation to the population, cleaning-up operations, and protection of the cultural heritage. 3 https://civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu/what/civil-protection/resceu_en. 4 COM(2026) 330 final, Communication from the Commission on integrated wildfire risk management, https://ec.europa.
